components.gap: The Church 1940 allocation of N-a-071 is not complete: N-a-071-S01-PRESENTATION and N-a-071-S01-PROOF are partial (see their gaps); N-a-071-S01-BRIDGE is covered. Church's system is presented as its own source presentation, separately from the relational calculus (no hybrid replacement); the Henkin 1950, Andrews 2002 and Shapiro 1991 allocations belong to units ED26-REQ-N-a-071-02..04 and are not judged here.

Not every item of Church 1940's required extent is presented. Omitted: (1) the justificatory and normative framing on p.56 - that the partial incorporation of lambda-conversion has certain advantages from the point of view of type theory and is offered as being of interest on that basis, whatever may be thought of the finally satisfactory character of the theory of types as a foundation for logic and mathematics (only the impossibility of a complete incorporation is reported, w02-p02-040 body lines 911-913); (2) the historical claims: p.56, that for features not connected with lambda-conversion the formulation is heavily indebted to Whitehead and Russell, Hilbert and Ackermann, Hilbert and Bernays and their forerunners (nn.3-5); n.1, citing Carnap's Abriss der Logistik sec.9, that the simple theory of types was suggested as a modification of Russell's ramified theory by Chwistek (1921, 1922) and Ramsey (1926); n.10's reference of the typical-ambiguity device to the Prefatory Statement of Principia vol.2; (3) the source example of sec.1, p.56, 'iota iota(iota iota) for ((iota iota)(iota iota))', which def:p02-w02-p02-040-church-types (body lines 42-45) replaces by an example the source does not contain ('iota(iota iota) abbreviates (iota(iota iota))'); (4) the sec.1, p.57 qualification that the matter of interpretation is irrelevant to the abstract construction of the theory and that other, quite different interpretations are possible 'formal consistency assumed' (body lines 166-168 keep only that the source admits other interpretations); (5) the sec.4, p.61 justification that the formal/syntactical-theorem distinction is a necessary part of using a known language (English) to set up another, more exact language (w02-p02-041 body lines 605-615 report the distinction without it). Supply these claims, the source's own example and these qualifications at their locators.

Not every proof required by the presentation is supplied with the source's exact hypotheses. (1) The source states (sec.6, p.64) that 26^iota', 26^iota'', ... are consequences of Axioms 1-6^alpha and 8; the written derivation (w02-p02-040 annex lines 570-650) also uses Axiom 7 (through 28^alpha and 27^iota), and def:p02-w02-p02-040-church-26-axiom-7 (body lines 489-500) leaves 'whether Axiom 7 can be removed' unsettled: a derivation of 26^iota', 26^iota'', ... from Axioms 1-6^alpha and 8 alone, or a proof that the source's claim fails, is owed. (2) The source derives (sec.2, p.59) from the independence of the axiom of infinity (sec.4) that the same-type predecessor P_alpha'alpha' cannot be defined without descriptions; the handbook reports this and says it does not prove it (w02-p02-041 body lines 617-632; w02b-p02-034 body lines 624-633); the derivation (or a demonstration that the stated inference fails) is owed. (3) The consequences the source attaches to the further axiom p = q (as propositions) implying p = q (p.61: only two propositions; with 10^alphabeta, classes identifiable with propositional functions) are reported (w02-p02-040 body lines 316-319) without derivation.

defect_observations: w02-p02-040 body lines 42-45: the third type-abbreviation example ('iota(iota iota) abbreviates (iota(iota iota))') is not in Church 1940; the source's example (p.56) is 'iota iota(iota iota) for ((iota iota)(iota iota))'. Church's p.64 announcement ('consequences of 1-6^alpha and 8') is not established by the source's own proof (pp.66-67 use 28^alpha, whose proof on p.65 uses 27^alpha, which is Axiom 7 at alpha = iota); the handbook's warning def:p02-w02-p02-040-church-26-axiom-7 records this accurately but leaves the question open.
